newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UNHCR asks Angola to agree Rwandan refugee airlift.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR asks Angola to agree Rwandan refugee airlift.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency UNHCR appealed to Angola on Tuesday to agree to open a humanitarian corridor from its border into neighbouring Zaire to allow an airlift of Rwandan Hutu refugees stranded there.
Spokeswoman Pam O'Toole said UNHCR needed Luanda's approval to reach the refugees, in an isolated border region of Zaire, from Angola and airlift them to Rwanda from Angolan territory.

Angola has a long border with Zaire, where Tutsi-dominated rebels are marching on the capital Kinshasa. It says up to 17,000 Hutus are camped across its northern frontier with Zaire but has previously denied the UNHCR cross-border access to the area.

Aid workers say the Hutus are seeking refuge with Angola's former rebel UNITA movement which controls vast areas along the border. Zaire's embattled President Mobutu Sese Seko backed UNITA during Angola's 20-year civil war that ended in 1994.
O'Toole said UNHCR on Monday found a group of some 500 refugees just across the border in Zaire. The agency had also located another group of 12,000 Rwandan Hutus farther inside Zaire.
UNHCR hoped to airlift the refugees from Dundo, a border area controlled by the Angolan government.

The Rwandans in Zaire are the residue of some two million Hutus who fled their country in fear of reprisal for 1994's Hutu-led genocide of Tutsis. More than half a million went home late last year but up to 300,000 fled deeper into Zaire.
